rows.title: Syntactic Interface Overfitting in Web Agents: Why do learned skills bind to literal text envelopes rather than semantic intents?
rows.exact_prediction: Skills acquired with varied syntactic envelopes (but same semantics) will show higher transfer utility to native function-calling executors than skills acquired with a single envelope, under matched semantic content and task distribution.
rows.falsifier_expression: Run the AWM skill acquisition with varied syntactic envelopes (e.g., paraphrased WebArena envelopes) and test transfer utility to native function-calling executors. If utility remains low, the syntactic-binding hypothesis is falsified.
rows.endpoint_headroom_requirement: Utility must be significantly below 0.756 (the restored utility) when the envelope is mismatched, and significantly above 0.319 (the collapsed utility) when the envelope is varied during acquisition.
